utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a lack of confidence among the parties, and the parties -- both parties do not trust the other. One party thinks that the other is preparing to attack, and they are suspicious of one another. There is an attempt to have talks, and when a killing occurs, as far as I know the HVO did not have any plan beforehand to attack anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. I could go on for hours on this document, but I see that there is a sentence on the use of arms by the Muslim forces, two mortars. When they say that, do they have reliable information that shows that the Muslim were is using mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They had reliable information. I read and talked about this. They used Maljutkas and mortars. They were very well-armed, basically. They had respectable weapons in homes, and they had exact plans, who would fire at whom and when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a small detail in the document. Apparently they used a Sagger anti-tank missile. I don't know what that is. If it is mentioned in the report, then it means that it was used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, but I do know that they had Maljutkas. This is a Russian anti-tank weapon. And I know that the HVO used attack -- a tank in those battles. I don't know whether the tank was hit and what happened to it, but there's no reason to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I'm going to take you back to some of -- a little bit back in time since you seem to be more willing now to talk about some of the issues involving things that were in place before your arrival. You say there was no HVO plan to attack Prozor, and you also talked about the killing of the HVO soldier as the trigger, but we've already -- today we've looked at the Boban or Kordic order appointing the HVO -- the municipal HVO for Prozor. We've looked at the Markesic report on the tensions created by raising the Croatian flag, General Petkovic's order to block the TO forces on the 20th of October, 1992, and then this HVO demand to the Muslims that they accept the civilian and military structures of the HVO there in Prozor. So -- I mean, we can talk about whether, you know, the ABiH made a plan to attack the HVO, but the fact is that by the 23rd, the 24th of October, 1992, the HVO was going to assert its authority, both civilian and military, over Prozor, no matter what; isn't that the truth? That the bottom line is that the HVO was going to control this municipality militarily and -- and the civilian, and that if a -- the conflict that resulted was a result of that bottom line for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, do I not agree with you, and from hundreds of documents that I have reviewed and that have been admitted into evidence, and on the basis of everything that I sought to find out and from what is written in the documents in proportion to the number -- numbers in the population, let us organise the military and civilian authority. I have seen plans that were captured in the conflict, plans of the BH Army, plan A for the Chetniks and plan B for the HVO. I'm talking about the documents that I am familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you're referring to this ABiH plan to attack Prozor. The fact is that if the ABiH did nothing, if the Muslims did nothing, then they were just going to have to sit back and accept HVO military and civilian control over -- over the municipality of Prozor. Isn't that how it was? Isn't that again why the conflict happened?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand proportionality in that sense. To me it means a distribution, a sharing of military and civilian duties, and that is in my view the best way to reach an agreement, if there is a proportion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You know, a lot of times in your testimony, General, you've said that, "They can't give us what is ours," you know, in referring to the rights of Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. "They can't give it to us. We own it already. It's not for them to give." But really, you're just proposing the very same thing, aren't you? What you're saying to the Muslims, what they're saying to the Muslim people in Prozor is, "We've set up a separate authority here. It's called the municipal HVO, and we are going to give you proportional representation in our structure, but we insist that you accept our structure." The Muslims did not accept the structure in Prozor and that's why the conflict erupted; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you why the conflict erupted, but, sir, I do not think that when we proposed a Joint Command it was again proportional. And as there were more Muslims, they would get more seats. The proportionality that we offered is not offering power to somebody. We wanted proportionality in all the structures in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Unfortunately, what we offered, we were never given. HVO units which were under the command of the BH Army did not have their representatives in the commands of the ABiH except for rare exceptions, and when it comes to the authorities, even less so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I'm going to move to the next exhibit that we'll probably finish with today. P00640.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we look at this document, Mr. Stringer has put a question to you which was very interesting and which could perhaps resolve the problem to see whether there was a plan or not. He started from the idea that the HVO wanted to take control of the Prozor municipality and that in view of that the ABiH could have reacted by planning an attack, which could perhaps explain many things, and I am using the conditional. But in Mr. Stringer's hypothesis, the HVO wanted to take political control of Prozor, and this requires some explanations on your part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, the HVO did put Prozor under its control after the conflict, and in those conflicts once it gained control it said, "We don't want control. We want proportionality." And Jure Smidt says, "We cannot come to an agreement with these people in Rama. Let's go to Bugojno and with high-level structures we can reach an agreement." That, in my view, cannot be interpreted in other way except a reflection of the constant desire to have talks and a commonality based on the principle of equality in rights and proportionality. I tell you that was not the idea of Alija Izetbegovic nor the large majority of Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina, excluding Tuzla and some others. They believed that Bosnia-Herzegovina was theirs. If they couldn't take it from the Serbs, they wanted to take it from us. That is my assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling us that HVO took control of Prozor, but you say after the conflict, which means that before the events of the 24th of October, there was no political control by the HVO over Prozor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They were proportionally represented in the authorities, and they talked. And when the conflict broke out and when they put Rama under their control, again they started -- wanted to have talks. And what did I do? I again achieved joint authority being established, which functioned for at least a year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to Mr. Stringer for him to complete his point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the next document it's probably best left for tomorrow rather than starting a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Fine. You're absolutely right. So we'll meet again, as you know, tomorrow at 2.15, and as usual, I wish everyone a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of August, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
